grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('yakavakwa')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'yakavakwa' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('reruvara')
grammar_notes.content: This passage uses colour vocabulary such as 'reruvara'. Shona has three traditional core colour adjectives that change their prefix slightly to match the noun they describe: '-chena' (white/clean, e.g., 'ruvara ruchena' or 'shangu chena'), '-tema / nhema' (black/dark, e.g., 'mota nhema' or 'ruvara rutema'), and '-tsvuku' (red/bright brown, e.g., 'mota tsvuku' or 'ruvara rutsvuku'). For other colours like green ('girinhi'), blue ('bhuruu'), or orange ('orenji'), speakers typically say 'ruvara rwe-' ('the colour of...') followed by the colour name, as in 'ruvara rwegirinhi' (green).
grammar_notes.rule: Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('pasi')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'pasi'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

cultural_notes.title: Double-Storey Suburban Architecture & Cycling ('Bhasikoro')
cultural_notes.content: Newly developed residential suburbs around Zimbabwean cities feature double-storey homes ('imba yakavakwa ichienda mudenga') with wide sunlit windows ('mafafitera mahombe') and spacious yards where children ride bicycles ('mabhasikoro').

active_exercises.prompt: If a farmer says 'Gore rino takawana goho guru pamunda pedu', what happened?
options: They are waiting for the rain to start next month
The river flooded and washed away the bridge
A strong wind blew from the east all afternoon
They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
active_exercises.correct_answer: They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
active_exercises.explanation: 'Takawana' = 'we obtained/got', 'goho guru' = 'a big harvest', 'pamunda pedu' = 'from our field'.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Mhepo iri kuvhuvhuta uye mvura ichanaya manheru.'
options: The wind is blowing and it will rain in the evening.
The river is full of water after yesterday's heavy rain.
Tall green trees grow along the sides of the mountain.
The dog barked outside when it saw the visitors.
active_exercises.correct_answer: The wind is blowing and it will rain in the evening.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Mhepo iri kuvhuvhuta' = 'The wind is blowing', 'uye' = 'and', 'mvura ichanaya manheru' = 'it will rain in the evening'.

active_exercises.prompt: Your friend just passed her driving test! What do you say to congratulate her in Shona?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Makorokoto!' means 'Congratulations!' and 'nekubudirira kwako' means 'on your success'.
